<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/../src/Accessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/JsonAccessor.php';

use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\EnvAccessor;
use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\JsonAccessor;

$failures = 0;
function check(string $name, bool $ok): void
{
    global $failures;
    echo ($ok ? "ok   " : "FAIL ") . $name . "\n";
    if (!$ok) {
        $failures++;
    }
}

$env = new EnvAccessor("HOST=localhost\nPORT=3000\n");
check('reads KEY=value lines', $env->get('HOST') === 'localhost' && $env->get('PORT') === '3000');

$env = new EnvAccessor("# a comment\n\nKEY=value\n");
check('skips blank lines and comments', $env->all() === ['KEY' => 'value']);

$env = new EnvAccessor("A=\"one two\"\nB='three'\n");
check('strips one pair of matching quotes', $env->get('A') === 'one two' && $env->get('B') === 'three');

$env = new EnvAccessor('KEY=value');
check('answers the fallback for a key that is not there', $env->get('MISSING', 'none') === 'none' && $env->has('KEY') && !$env->has('MISSING'));

$json = new JsonAccessor('{"name":"x","count":3}');
check('json keeps the string values of an object', $json->all() === ['name' => 'x']);

exit($failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

input.title: EnvAccessor strips a leading `export` only when a key follows it, in both packages
input.rationale: `export KEY=value` is read as `KEY=value`. The prefix is `export` plus spaces or tabs, removed after the line is trimmed, and only when the next character is neither whitespace nor `=` (regex `^export[ \t]+(?=[^\s=])`). That keeps `export = 1`, `export=1` and `exportKEY=2` meaning what they meant before, so the change adds a form and takes none away. `[ \t]` is spelled out, not `\s`, so JS and PHP match the same characters (JS `\s` is wider than PCRE `\s` without /u). Made in `packages/js` and `packages/php` in the same change, as ADR-1 requires, with the same two tests in each.
input.alternatives: Strip a bare `export ` prefix with no lookahead: simpler, but `export = 1` would stop meaning a key named `export` and become a skipped line, a silent change to an existing input. Parse shell syntax properly (`export A=1 B=2`, `export -n`, escapes): out of scope for a plain stdlib-only accessor and not asked for. Strip `export` case-insensitively: the shell keyword is lowercase only, so `Export X=1` stays a key named `Export X`.

content.text:
`EnvAccessor` now reads `export KEY=value` as `KEY=value`, in both the JS and PHP packages. Both test suites pass.

- **Parity:** I changed both packages because ADR-1 says a behavior change goes into both in the same change. This repo has no `parity-vectors.json`, so there were no shared vectors to update.
- **The rule:** a leading `export` followed by spaces or tabs is dropped, but only when a key comes next. Other lines behave as before: `export = 1` is still a key named `export`, and `exportKEY=2` is still `exportKEY`. `export KEY` with no `=` is still skipped, and so is a commented-out `# export X=1`.
- **Tests:** I added two tests with the same cases in each package. One covers `export KEY=value` with extra spaces, a tab and a quoted value. The other covers lines that only look like an export.
- **Where:** the code is in `env-accessor.ts` and `EnvAccessor.php`, the tests in `env-accessor.test.ts` and `run.php`.

I recorded the rule and the alternatives I turned down as ADR-2. It is `proposed`, so it still needs someone to accept it. The record tool suggested superseding ADR-1, which I didn't do, because ADR-2 doesn't replace it.

Nothing is committed. `.mnema/` has new untracked files from this session's key: a `.pub` key file and a `tails/` directory. Commit them with the code changes. I'll commit if you want.

The record also reported that this session's key founded a separate identity, `mnid:e5c436c2`, next to the existing `mnid:3b2c3f61`. If that's you on another key, the record will count you twice. The fix is to run `mnema key request --anchor mnid:3b2c3f61` yourself and enroll the printed line from a machine in the original identity. Otherwise there's nothing to do.
